description: Machine-readable validation rules for extraction quality (from EXTRACTION_FIELD_QUALITY_FRAMEWORK_2026-02-28.md)

severity_levels.critical: Field is invalid and breaks interpretation. Must be fixed.
severity_levels.error: Field violates constraints. Should be flagged for re-extraction.
severity_levels.warning: Field is usable but has quality concerns. Flag for review.
severity_levels.info: Field is fine but could be improved.

rules.description: Antecedent must not be null or empty
rules.error_message: Antecedent cannot be null or empty string

rules.description: Antecedent must not be vague or use catch-all terms
rules.error_message: Antecedent uses vague terms like 'environmental features' or 'various'. Must be specific.

rules.description: Antecedent must not contain outcome language. Expanded set includes: improved, enhanced, facilitated, promoted, reduced, decreased, modulated, suppressed
rules.error_message: Antecedent contains outcome language (e.g., 'improved', 'better'). Must describe the environmental condition, not the result.

rules.description: Demographic used as antecedent without factorial design (confound risk)
rules.warning_message: Demographic variable used as IV. Check: is this the actual independent variable (architectural feature) or a moderator?

severity_conditions.ERROR: article_family='experimental' AND antecedent is bare demographic AND no_factorial_design
severity_conditions.WARNING: article_family='observational' AND demographic used as moderator

rules.description: Antecedent should be reasonably detailed (not too short or too long)
rules.warning_message: Antecedent length unusual. Should be 5-500 characters.

rules.description: Consequent must not be null or empty
rules.error_message: Consequent cannot be null or empty

rules.description: Consequent must not be a restatement of antecedent
rules.error_message: Consequent is too similar to antecedent (>60% token overlap). Consequent should describe the outcome, not restate the IV.

rules.description: Consequent must align with stated outcome_domain
rules.error_message: Consequent does not match stated outcome_domain. Check: is outcome_domain correct, or is consequent description wrong?

rules.description: Consequent should align with stated measure_type
rules.warning_message: Consequent description does not match stated measure_type.

rules.description: Consequent should be concise but descriptive
rules.warning_message: Consequent length unusual. Should be 3-300 characters.

direction.description: Effect direction: increase, decrease, no_effect, mixed

rules.description: Direction must be one of: increase, decrease, no_effect, mixed, null
rules.error_message: Invalid direction value. Must be one of: increase, decrease, no_effect, mixed. Do NOT use synonyms like 'enhance', 'facilitate', 'modulate', 'affect'.

rules.description: If direction is 'mixed', effect_size must be null
rules.error_message: Direction='mixed' cannot be paired with numeric effect_size. Either: (1) use 'mixed' with null ES, or (2) report separate findings per condition.

rules.description: Direction must match effect_size sign
rules.error_message: Direction does not match effect_size sign. E.g., direction='increase' but effect_size=-0.45.

rules.description: Direction should align with p_value significance for empirical claims
rules.warning_message: Direction implies significant effect, but p_value >= 0.05 (not significant). Verify reported values.

rules.description: Empirical claims must have a direction
rules.error_message: Direction is null but claim_type indicates empirical finding. Must specify direction.

rules.description: claim_type must be a recognized value
rules.error_message: Invalid claim_type. Must be one of the allowed values.

rules.description: claim_type='empirical_finding' must have statistics
rules.error_message: claim_type='empirical_finding' but no statistics (p_value, effect_size, test_statistic) provided.

rules.description: Check consistency between article_type and claim_type distribution
rules.warning_message: Article type and claim type combination seems unusual. Verify extraction is correct.

rules.description: measure_type must be one of the allowed values
rules.error_message: Invalid measure_type. Must be one of: self_report, behavioral, physiological, cognitive_task, observational, mixed.

rules.description: Empirical claims should have measure_type specified
rules.error_message: measure_type is null for empirical claim. Should specify how outcome was measured.

rules.description: measure_type should align with consequent field
rules.warning_message: measure_type does not match consequent description.

rules.description: p_value must be in range [0, 1]
rules.error_message: p_value out of range [0, 1]. Verify value.

rules.description: p_value stored as string (e.g., '< 0.05') instead of numeric
rules.warning_message: p_value is a string. Should be numeric float for consistency.

rules.description: p_value should be consistent with direction
rules.warning_message: p_value >= 0.05 (not significant) but direction suggests significant effect. Verify.

rules.description: Empirical findings should have p_value
rules.error_message: p_value is null for empirical claim. APA 7th ed. requires p-value reporting.

rules.description: Narrative/theoretical claims should not have p_value
rules.condition: claim_type in ['narrative', 'theoretical_proposition'] and p_value is not null
rules.warning_message: p_value present for narrative/theoretical claim. Unusual.

rules.description: effect_size must be in valid range for its type
rules.error_message: effect_size out of valid range for its effect_size_type.

rules.description: effect_size sign must match direction
rules.error_message: effect_size sign does not match direction.

rules.description: Empirical findings should report effect_size
rules.error_message: effect_size is null for empirical claim. APA 7th ed. recommends effect size reporting.

rules.description: effect_size_type must be specified if effect_size is present
rules.error_message: effect_size is present but effect_size_type is null.

effect_size_type.description: Name of the effect size statistic

rules.description: effect_size_type must be specified if effect_size is present
rules.error_message: effect_size is present but effect_size_type is null.

rules.description: Use standard names for effect size types
rules.warning_message: effect_size_type should use standard naming convention.

rules.description: sample_size must be positive integer
rules.error_message: sample_size must be a positive integer.

rules.description: Empirical findings should report sample_size
rules.warning_message: sample_size is null for empirical claim. APA 7th ed. requires N reporting.

rules.description: Narrative claims should not have sample_size
rules.condition: claim_type in ['narrative', 'theoretical_proposition'] and sample_size is not null
rules.info_message: sample_size present for narrative claim. Unusual but not invalid.

sample_size_source.description: Source of sample_size information (reported, inferred, or estimated)

rules.description: sample_size_source must be one of allowed values
rules.warning_message: sample_size_source has unrecognized value. Should be 'reported', 'inferred', or 'estimated'.

rules.description: When sample_size is present, source should be specified
rules.condition: sample_size is not null and sample_size_source is null
rules.info_message: sample_size is present but sample_size_source not specified. Recommended to track origin.

rules.description: Estimated sample sizes lower confidence
rules.info_message: sample_size was estimated rather than directly reported. May reduce finding reliability.

stimulus_description.description: Description of stimulus or environmental manipulation used in finding

rules.description: Empirical claims should specify primary stimulus type
rules.error_message: stimulus_description present but primary_type is missing. Must specify visual_scene, soundscape, thermal, olfactory, spatial, lighting, material, or mixed.

rules.description: Stimulus description should include at least one component
rules.warning_message: stimulus_description present but components array is empty. Should describe what stimulus elements compose the manipulation.

rules.description: Stimulus description must specify delivery method
rules.error_message: stimulus_description present but delivery_method not specified. Must be in_situ, VR, photo, video, audio, or imagined.

stimulus_images.description: Array of images documenting the stimulus

rules.description: Stimulus images should have recognized image types
rules.warning_message: Image has unrecognized image_type. Should be photo, rendering, diagram, floor_plan, or graph.

rules.description: Stimulus images should reference paper figure
rules.info_message: Stimulus image does not reference a figure in the paper. Helpful for traceability.

theory_commitments.description: How finding relates to theories (tests, extends, contradicts, assumes, proposes)

rules.description: Empirical/causal findings should link to at least one theory
rules.warning_message: Finding does not link to any theory even though article presents theoretical framework. Should specify which theory the finding tests/extends/contradicts.

rules.description: theory_commitment commitment_type must be valid
rules.error_message: theory_commitment has invalid commitment_type. Must be tests, extends, contradicts, assumes, or proposes.

rules.description: Each theory_commitment must specify what claim is being engaged
rules.error_message: theory_commitment missing specific_claim. Should state the precise claim from the theory being tested/extended.

rules.description: specific_claim should be substantive
rules.warning_message: specific_claim is too brief. Should be a complete statement of the theoretical claim (min. 10 characters).

mechanism_chain.description: Step-by-step mechanism linking antecedent to consequent

rules.description: Causal claims should explain mechanism with at least 2 steps
rules.warning_message: Causal claim lacks mechanism_chain or has fewer than 2 steps. Should explain how antecedent leads to consequent through intermediate constructs.

rules.description: mechanism_chain step numbers must be sequential starting from 1
rules.error_message: mechanism_chain steps are not sequential (e.g., 1, 2, 3). Steps must be consecutive integers starting at 1.

rules.description: mechanism_type must be recognized
rules.error_message: mechanism_chain step has invalid mechanism_type. Must be neural, perceptual, cognitive, affective, behavioral, or physiological.

rules.description: evidence_strength should indicate basis for mechanism
rules.warning_message: mechanism_chain step has invalid or missing evidence_strength. Should indicate if mechanism is direct, indirect, theoretical, or assumed.

rules.description: molecule_ids should follow naming convention
rules.info_message: molecule_id should use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE format (e.g., VISUAL_COMPLEXITY_AROUSAL).

rules.description: molecule_ids should be registered in rasa_attractors.json
rules.info_message: Consider registering this molecule_id in rasa_attractors.json for broader use.

rules.description: All fields in required_fields should exist in the finding
rules.error_message: success_conditions specifies required_fields that are missing from the finding.

rules.description: If theory_link_expected is true, theory_links should be non-empty
rules.warning_message: success_conditions expects theory link but theory_links is null or empty.

rules.description: If mechanism_expected is true, mechanism or mechanism_chain should be present
rules.warning_message: success_conditions expects mechanism but neither mechanism nor mechanism_chain is present.

instruments_used.description: Measurement instruments or scales used in the finding

rules.description: instrument_id should match registered instruments where possible
rules.warning_message: instrument_id does not match any registered instrument. Consider adding to instruments registry.

rules.description: Instrument names must be specific, not vague or generic
rules.error_message: instrument name is too vague (e.g., just 'questionnaire', 'scale', 'survey'). Must specify the actual instrument (e.g., 'Perceived Stress Scale', 'State-Trait Anxiety Inventory').

rules.description: construct_measured should be specified for instruments
rules.warning_message: Instrument missing construct_measured. Should specify what psychological/physiological construct it measures.

rules.description: Instruments should report reliability metrics when available
rules.info_message: Good practice to report Cronbach's alpha or test-retest reliability for instruments used.

rules.description: CI must be [lower, upper] array of two numeric values
rules.error_message: confidence_interval must be [lower, upper] with two numeric values.

rules.description: CI lower bound must be less than upper bound
rules.error_message: confidence_interval lower bound >= upper bound.

rules.description: effect_size should fall within CI
rules.warning_message: effect_size is outside the reported CI. Verify values.

rules.description: CI width should be reasonable
rules.warning_message: confidence_interval is very wide, indicating low precision.

test_statistic.description: Name and value of statistical test

rules.description: test_statistic should follow standard format
rules.warning_message: test_statistic format unusual. Expected: t(df), F(df1, df2), χ²(df), etc.

rules.description: Degrees of freedom should be consistent with sample_size
rules.warning_message: Degrees of freedom seem inconsistent with reported sample_size.

rules.description: test_statistic value should be consistent with p_value
rules.rough_rule: if p < 0.001 then |test_stat_value| should be substantial
rules.warning_message: test_statistic value seems inconsistent with p_value.

rules.description: test_statistic should be present for empirical findings
rules.condition: sample_size is not null and test_statistic is null
rules.info_message: test_statistic is null despite sample_size being present. If from table, should extract test_statistic.

causal_tier.description: Pearl causal design hierarchy (P5). Determines permitted causal language: EXPERIMENTAL allows 'X causes Y', QUASI allows 'X likely contributes to Y', CORRELATIONAL allows only 'X is associated with Y'.

rules.description: Causal tier must not be null for empirical findings
rules.condition: causal_tier is null AND claim_type in ['empirical_finding', 'causal', 'associational']
rules.error_message: causal_tier is null but claim_type indicates empirical data. Must specify causal design tier.

rules.description: Causal language in finding text must match causal_tier
rules.error_message: Finding text uses causal language (e.g., 'causes', 'leads to') but causal_tier is CORRELATIONAL. Correlational designs support only 'is associated with'.
rules.fix_suggestion: Either upgrade causal_tier to match language (if design supports it) or downgrade language to 'is associated with'.

rules.description: EXPERIMENTAL tier should include evidence of manipulation/intervention
rules.condition: causal_tier == 'EXPERIMENTAL' AND (mechanism is null OR antecedent does not mention manipulation keywords)
rules.warning_message: Causal tier is EXPERIMENTAL but finding lacks clear evidence of manipulation. Verify study design supports experimental classification.

scope_conditions.description: Cartwright scope conditions (P4). Specifies the populations, settings, and contexts where this finding holds. Unknown scope ≠ universal scope.

rules.description: Scope conditions required for empirical findings with at least 2 dimensions specified
rules.condition: claim_type in ['empirical_finding', 'causal', 'associational'] AND scope_conditions is null
rules.error_message: scope_conditions is null for empirical finding. Must specify at least 2 scope dimensions (setting, population, climate, duration, measurement_type).

rules.description: Setting should not be vague or overly general
rules.warning_message: Setting is vague ('indoor', 'outdoor', 'lab', 'field'). Specify setting type more precisely (e.g., 'office building', 'university laboratory', 'residential homes in coastal California').

rules.description: Population should be specific enough for replication
rules.warning_message: Population is underspecified. Should include demographic descriptors (age range, profession, education level, cultural context).

rules.description: Explicitly track unknown scope dimensions per Cartwright principle
rules.condition: scope_conditions exists AND scope_unknown_dimensions is empty
rules.info_message: Consider explicitly listing which scope dimensions are unknown in scope_unknown_dimensions array. Per Cartwright: unknown scope ≠ universal scope.

justification_status.description: Haack foundherentist classification (P2). GROUNDED = independent empirical anchor + coherence. COHERENT_ONLY = fits web but no independent evidence (Haack warning). UNJUSTIFIED = no support. EXPERIENTIAL_CLAIM = direct observation without theoretical framing.

rules.description: Justification status should be specified for all findings
rules.warning_message: justification_status is null. Should be specified to track grounding level.

rules.description: GROUNDED status requires cited empirical data
rules.condition: justification_status == 'GROUNDED' AND (p_value is null AND effect_size is null AND sample_size is null)
rules.error_message: justification_status is GROUNDED but no empirical data (p_value, effect_size, or sample_size) is reported. GROUNDED requires independent empirical evidence.
rules.fix_suggestion: Either extract the empirical statistics from the paper, or downgrade to COHERENT_ONLY if no direct empirical support exists in this paper.

rules.description: Flag for review if >30% of article findings are COHERENT_ONLY
rules.info_message: More than 30% of this article's findings are COHERENT_ONLY (no independent empirical support). Flag for review: article may be over-relying on theoretical coherence without empirical anchoring.

rules.description: EXPERIENTIAL_CLAIM should be directly quoted from text
rules.warning_message: justification_status is EXPERIENTIAL_CLAIM but no direct quote is provided. Experiential claims should be supported by direct text evidence.

defeat_relationships.description: Pollock defeat relationships (P1). Any known rebutting or undercutting defeaters for this finding, either reported in the paper or discovered across the corpus.

rules.description: High-credence findings should document any known defeaters
rules.warning_message: Finding has high credence (≥0.70) but no defeat_relationships documented and defeater_search_status is not 'none_reported'. Should actively search for and document any known defeaters.

rules.description: Each defeat relationship must have substantive description
rules.error_message: Defeat relationship description is too brief (<10 characters). Must provide substantive description of how this defeater attacks the finding.

rules.description: Defeat severity should correspond to effect on credence
rules.info_message: Defeat relationship marked as 'strong' but finding credence is >0.50. Consider whether credence should be lower given strong defeater.

defeater_search_status.description: Mayo severe testing status (P3). Whether defeaters (null results, boundary conditions, replication failures) were actively sought and what was found.

rules.description: Empirical findings should specify defeater search status
rules.condition: defeater_search_status is null AND claim_type in ['empirical_finding', 'causal', 'associational']
rules.warning_message: defeater_search_status is null for empirical finding. Should indicate whether defeaters were actively sought (severe testing per Mayo).

rules.description: If defeaters_found, defeat_relationships array must not be empty
rules.condition: defeater_search_status == 'defeaters_found' AND (defeat_relationships is null OR defeat_relationships.length == 0)
rules.error_message: defeater_search_status is 'defeaters_found' but defeat_relationships array is empty. Must document the defeaters that were found.
rules.fix_suggestion: Add the found defeaters to defeat_relationships array, or change status to 'none_reported' if no defeaters actually exist.

rules.description: not_searched status should be rare and justified
rules.info_message: defeater_search_status is 'not_searched' for causal/empirical finding. For severe testing (Mayo), defeaters should be actively searched. Recommend: change to 'none_reported' after conducting search, or document reasons search was not performed.

source_quality_indicators.description: Longino+Cartwright source quality assessment (P6). Quality-weighted evidence assessment: rigor, independence, replication, commitment penalty.

rules.description: Independence flag should be specified when multiple studies on same relationship exist
rules.warning_message: independence_flag is null. Should specify whether this study is independent from other studies on the same IV→DV (different lab, paradigm, population per Longino).

rules.description: Blinding status must be logically consistent with causal design
rules.error_message: Blinding status is 'double_blind' but causal_tier is CORRELATIONAL. Blinding is only possible in experimental designs with interventions. Correlational/observational studies cannot be blinded.
rules.fix_suggestion: Change blinding to 'not_applicable' or 'unblinded' for correlational studies.

rules.description: Replication status should inform credence/justification assessment
rules.info_message: Replication status is 'failed_replication' but finding credence is >0.60. Consider whether credence should be lower given failed replication.

rules.description: Exploratory studies should note Longino commitment penalty
rules.warning_message: Study type is 'exploratory' (receives half Longino commitment penalty) but credence is >0.65. Consider whether credence appropriately reflects exploratory status (typically capped lower than confirmatory).

conflict_type.description: Cartwright conflict typology (P10). When this finding conflicts with other findings on the same IV→DV, classify the disagreement type. CONTRADICTS = opposite conclusions, same scope. PRECISION_DIFFERENCE = same direction, different magnitude (not a true conflict).

rules.description: CONTRADICTS should be further typed when possible
rules.condition: conflict_type == 'CONTRADICTS' AND (direction == 'mixed' OR mechanism is null)
rules.warning_message: conflict_type is generic 'CONTRADICTS'. When possible, specify further using DIRECTION_CONFLICT, BOUNDARY_VIOLATION, or PRECISION_DIFFERENCE to clarify the nature of the conflict.

rules.description: Conflict type must be accompanied by description of conflicting finding
rules.condition: conflict_type is not null AND conflict_type != null AND (defeat_relationships.length == 0 OR defeat_relationships.items(description is null))
rules.error_message: conflict_type is specified but no corresponding defeat_relationships with description. Must document which other finding this conflicts with and how.

rules.description: PRECISION_DIFFERENCE is not a true conflict per Cartwright
rules.info_message: conflict_type is PRECISION_DIFFERENCE (same direction, different magnitude). Per Cartwright, this is not a true conflict. Consider whether this should be resolved through effect size meta-analysis rather than conflict classification.

epistemic_level.description: Cartwright+Haack level classification (P9). Different epistemic levels have different evidential standards and credence thresholds.

rules.description: Epistemic level should be specified for all findings
rules.condition: epistemic_level is null AND claim_type in ['empirical_finding', 'causal', 'theoretical_proposition']
rules.warning_message: epistemic_level is null. Should specify to clarify evidentiary standard and credence ceiling.

rules.description: OBSERVATIONAL findings should not exceed credence ceiling of 0.85
rules.warning_message: epistemic_level is OBSERVATIONAL but credence is >0.85. Per Cartwright+Haack, observational claims have an evidential ceiling around 0.85 (no unobserved mechanisms can be claimed). Consider whether credence should be capped at this level.

rules.description: THEORETICAL epistemic level should include mechanism chain
rules.condition: epistemic_level == 'THEORETICAL' AND (mechanism is null AND mechanism_chain is null)
rules.warning_message: epistemic_level is THEORETICAL but no mechanism or mechanism_chain is provided. Theoretical claims should explain the underlying mechanism.

rules.description: EMPIRICAL findings should report statistics
rules.condition: epistemic_level == 'EMPIRICAL' AND (p_value is null AND effect_size is null AND test_statistic is null)
rules.warning_message: epistemic_level is EMPIRICAL but no statistics (p_value, effect_size, or test_statistic) are reported. Empirical claims should be grounded in quantitative results.

quality_scoring.description: How to compute field and finding quality scores

critical_fields.rationale: Semantic core of a finding. Without these, interpretation is impossible.

empirical_fields.rationale: Required for empirical claims, may be null for narrative claims.

supporting_fields.rationale: Quality modifiers. Important but not deal-breakers.

quality_scoring.family_thresholds_description: Quality acceptance thresholds vary by article family. Empirical/experimental papers (e.g., RCTs, surveys) have higher thresholds (0.70 blocking) because statistical rigor is primary. Qualitative and theoretical papers have lower thresholds (0.65 blocking) because robustness criteria differ. 'blocking' is the minimum for acceptance.

gates.description: Do not exceed 10% broken articles in a batch
Do not exceed 5% non-canonical direction values

panel_review_questions.title: Antecedent Specificity
panel_review_questions.question: Should antecedent specificity be measured against outcome vocabulary or independently?

panel_review_questions.title: Mixed Direction Findings
panel_review_questions.question: For mixed-direction findings, should we create separate findings per condition or flag for re-extraction?

panel_review_questions.title: Effect Size / Direction Tolerance
panel_review_questions.question: What is the tolerance for effect_size/direction consistency given rounding in reporting?

panel_review_questions.title: P-value Mandatoriness
panel_review_questions.question: Should null p_value be allowed for causal claims if direction and effect_size are clearly reported?

panel_review_questions.title: Claim Atomicity
panel_review_questions.question: How should we handle claims spanning multiple outcome domains (health AND cognition)?

consistency_rules.description: Cross-field validation rules that check relationships between multiple fields

rules.description: Direction vs. effect_size consistency
rules.condition: direction == 'increase' AND effect_size < 0 AND effect_size_type in ['Cohen\'s d', 'r', 'Hedges\' g']
rules.error_message: Direction is 'increase' but effect_size is negative. This is contradictory.
rules.fix_suggestion: Review the reported effect size and direction in the paper.

rules.description: P-value vs. direction consistency for causal claims
rules.condition: p_value > 0.05 AND direction in ['increase', 'decrease'] AND claim_type == 'causal'
rules.error_message: Effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) but direction implies a causal claim. This overclaims causality from non-significant data.
rules.fix_suggestion: Verify claim_type; if truly causal, effect should be p < 0.05. Otherwise downgrade to 'associational'.

rules.description: Causal claim in qualitative paper
rules.error_message: Article is qualitative but claim is marked 'causal'. Qualitative studies typically cannot establish causality.

rules.description: Effect size type specified but no effect size value
rules.condition: effect_size_type is not null AND effect_size is null
rules.error_message: effect_size_type is specified (e.g., 'Cohen\'s d') but effect_size is null. Incomplete data.
rules.fix_suggestion: Extract the numeric effect_size from the paper, or set effect_size_type to null if not reported.

rules.description: Underpowered causal claim
rules.error_message: Sample size is very small (N < 10) but claim is causal. This is likely underpowered.
rules.fix_suggestion: If sample is small, downgrade claim_type or note as exploratory.
